attributes.notes: REVERSAL EPISODE, recorded because the reasoning is reusable: StandardCamera was reverted mid-pass and then restored. Direct disassembly (fnasm.py) shows the target DOES relocate against the named lbl_* symbol for every one of the 9 labels substituted anywhere in this TU, which under the first advisory reading condemned all 5 wins. The FPR-allocation law resolves it: those named->anonymous relocations are the KNOWN COST (+1 real per site), not evidence of a wrong spelling, and the win comes from the constant leaving the FPR interference graph. Cost-model arithmetic for the marginal case, StandardCamera: 11 substituted sites, net real -28, therefore gross gain 39 = 3.55 diffs bought per 1 diff spent, comfortably over the law's break-even of 1. Its fuzzy dip (91.8428 -> 91.8177) is exactly the 11 relocation costs and did not move project fuzzy (97.91% either way). RULE-3 AUDIT (independently confirms claim.law.tu-wide-literalization-breaks-matched-sibling-pool-relocs' scoping corollary): 5 of the 9 substituted labels ARE also read by byte-identical siblings -- lbl_80345EC8 by get_pitch/recalc_lookat, lbl_80345F18 by ChangeWindow/get_pitch/recalc_lookat, lbl_80345F20 by get_pitch/recalc_lookat, lbl_80345F58 by get_yaw, lbl_80345F78 by get_pitch/get_yaw -- yet all 29 real-0 functions stayed at real 0 through every gate. Per-function line-range scoping, with the file-scope extern declaration and all sibling reads left untouched, is what makes that safe; a shared label is a reason not to sweep TU-wide, never a reason to skip a function. Separately, the camera-0 offsets recovered here land EXACTLY on game/camera.h's verified Camera layout with no deltas, a second-TU confirmation of that header.
